lines: Mind the wet ink. What can I help you find?
Come around this side of the table. The map is easier to read here.
If you have news about a road, start with where it went wrong.
Hello. Give me a moment to finish this coastline.
You look like you have been farther than the edge of my map.
Did you come for directions or to correct mine?
Set your bag down, but keep it off the parchment.
I can talk while the ink dries.
Tell me where you started, then we can work out where you ended.
Good timing. I was about to compare two very different reports.
If this is about a shortcut, I want the whole story first.
Come in. The compass has been better company than the weather.
I have room for one more road on this sheet.
Before you speak, look at the map and point to the trouble.
You are back. Did the route hold?
I was hoping someone with muddy boots would bring useful news.
Keep your sleeve clear of the ink and go ahead.
If you are lost, say so. It saves both of us time.
I have a question about the north road, if you have a moment.
All right. What needs marking?
